settings.intro: US CODE started as a way to keep one night from fading — Sina and Vida, a mural neither of us can un-see, and a memory we didn't want to just remember. We wanted to be able to play it back.
settings.caption: Sina & Vida — the night it started.
settings.body:
We were standing in front of a wall that looked like it was watching us back, and one of us said the kind of thing you only say at 2am: "I never want to forget this exact feeling." We took a video instead of a photo, because a photo freezes a moment and we wanted to keep the sound of it too.

A few weeks later we were still watching that clip more than we'd like to admit. That's the whole idea behind US CODE: most things you want to remember don't fit in a picture. So we built a shirt that holds the video instead — a real memory, tapped back into existence whenever you want it.
settings.demo_hint: This is the actual memory behind Drop 01 — click the eye like you'd tap the hem, and it plays back the same way it does on the shirt.

settings.heading: A memory, not a graphic.
settings.text: Every back print starts as a real photograph — someone's actual eyes, torn and layered by hand before it's screen-printed at true grain. Nothing on the shirt is generated.

settings.heading: Verified, not mass-produced.
settings.text: Each piece is numbered against its own NFC chip at print. When a drop's 300 are gone, that number closes — no restock, no reprint, ever.

settings.heading: Tap to remember.
settings.text: A hidden NFC chip sewn into the hem links to whatever you choose to keep behind it — a photo, a voice note, a video. Tap any modern phone to the hem and it plays back. No app needed.

settings.quote: Wear the memory. Not a graphic of one.

settings.heading: Know when the next drop lands.
